title: White Sox bulk up bullpen, acquire Huascar Brazobán from Mets
content:
The Athletic has live coverage of the 2026 MLB Trade Deadline.

In need of pitching of any kind, the Chicago White Sox agreed to acquire right-handed reliever Huascar Brazobán, one of the league’s best multi-inning men, in a trade with the New York Mets on Monday, league sources told The Athletic. The deal will send Double-A righty Gabe Davis and Triple-A righty Zach Franklin to New York, according to league sources who spoke on condition of anonymity because the deal is not yet official.

Brazobán is a versatile reliever, able to work as an opener and help in high-leverage situations. He became much more platoon neutral in 2026, limiting both left-handed and right-handed batters to a sub-.600 OPS. He has a 2.56 ERA over 52 2/3 innings in 46 appearances for the Mets, whose disappointing season has prompted a sell-off.

The 36-year-old, whom the Mets acquired in a trade with the Miami Marlins in 2024, experienced a mini breakout in 2025, solidifying a role as a trusted member of the bullpen. From there, things got better. He looked sharp in the World Baseball Classic and carried that into a big spring. Despite having a minor-league option, his spot for Opening Day became a certainty. In 2026, he evolved into one of the more reliable right-handers in the Mets’ bullpen, effective in back-to-back appearances and dependable for more than one inning.

Neither Davis, a fifth-round pick in last year’s draft, nor Franklin, a 10th round selection in 2023, ranked in Keith Law’s Top 20 White Sox prospects list for The Athletic. Davis was ranked No. 18 by MLB Pipeline.

At Oklahoma State, Davis dealt with myriad injuries, including an off-field incident that pushed him to the fifth round. He made his professional debut earlier this season at High-A Winston-Salem, posting a 2.63 ERA in eight starts before earning a promotion to Double A in May. Since then, he’s pitched to an 8.31 ERA over 10 starts. In three consecutive starts in mid-June, he allowed at least six runs and failed to complete four innings in any of them.

Franklin, who profiles as a multi-inning reliever like Brazobán, has been uneven at Triple A, his second season at that level. In May, he posted a 2.25 ERA over 10 games (12 innings) only to follow it up with a 6.10 mark in June over seven games. This came two months after bottoming out with a 8.38 ERA in April.

Brazobán figures to provide the White Sox with a boost. With Davis Martin, Sean Burke and Noah Schultz all on pace to exceed their career highs in innings, Brazobán figures to spell either of them in longer stints, particularly down the stretch. His acquisition, coupled with Chicago’s previous deal for Luis Castillo, should give the White Sox enough length as the club looks to win its first AL Central title since 2021.

What Brazobán lacks in strikeouts and whiffs, he more than makes up for by limiting hard contact. Among qualifying pitchers, Brazobán’s average exit velocity of 83.8 mph ranks fourth best in baseball. Relying on a sinker/changeup mix, his profile should bode well in October when homers reign supreme.

For Chicago, Brazobán is more than a rental. In just his first year of arbitration, Brazobán is owed about $310,000 for the remainder of the season. He’s under team control through 2029.

— The Athletic’s Johnny Flores Jr. contributed to this report.
